szoveg_eredeti:
LG CNS has built an artificial intelligence (AI) data center overseas for the first time as a domestic information technology (IT) company.

LG CNS announced on the 2nd that it completed the construction of a 30MW super-large (hyperscale) AI data center in Jakarta, Indonesia on the 1st and held a completion ceremony. This is the first case in which a domestic IT service company directly built an AI data center for an overseas customer. Before the completion of the data center, it also finished attracting customers 100%.

The project was ordered by KMG, a joint venture between Sinemas Group, a leading Indonesian company, and Korea Investment Real Asset Management last year. LG CNS has proven its data center design, construction, and operation (DBO) capabilities accumulated in Korea through its overseas performance.

The data center is designed with an expandable structure that can stably support high-performance computing (HPC) based on next-generation GPUs.

The key is specialized infrastructure tailored to AI servers that consume enormous heat and power. LG CNS has introduced a 'hybrid cooling structure' that uses air cooling and liquid cooling together. In the first stage of construction, an air-cooled cooling system was applied to lower the internal temperature by circulating air, and in the subsequent stage, a liquid cooling system that more precisely controls GPU heat generation will be added to provide a cooling infrastructure optimized for high-density AI server environments.

The power system is also built to cope with ultra-high density environments of 300 kW or more per rack (server storage box).

This is about 60 times the amount of power used in a typical data center rack, and power can be stably supplied to high-end AI computing resources that are equipped with multiple GPUs in one rack.

In addition, even if the supply of main power is cut off, it has a dual power grid system that guarantees uninterrupted operation 24 hours a day, 365 days a year through spare power.

This project fully applied the 'One LG' integrated solution, which unites core capabilities at the group level.

Focusing on LG CNS' DBO capabilities, LG Electronics' air conditioning system and LG Energy Solution's batteries were combined to provide integrated power, cooling, and energy infrastructure.

Through this, the group-level integrated competitiveness was implemented in overseas AI infrastructure projects and a strong reference was secured for future global orders.

LG CNS is currently in the process of designing to build a follow-up stage. When the additional construction is completed, the total power supply will be greatly expanded to 400MW, establishing itself as a large-scale AI data center representing Indonesia.

The company plans to actively respond to growing global AI infrastructure demand by expanding its AI data center business to major Asia-Pacific countries such as Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Japan, using this overseas construction experience and customer reference as a stepping stone.

LG CNS, a major data center operator in Korea, is speeding up its business portfolio diversification in addition to its overseas expansion.

It has continued to expand its scope, rather than staying in the traditional business of lending server space or building and operating centers instead. Examples include prefabricated data centers that build blocks quickly, subscription services that borrow expensive high-performance GPUs, and advanced cooling technology that cools hot servers with special liquids. In the future, the company plans to continue its sales growth by growing into a so-called "AI Factory" business that combines customized corporate AI platforms into one.

Hyun Shin-kyun, CEO of LG CNS, stressed, "The completion of the construction of the AI data center in Indonesia is an achievement that LG CNS has provided overseas customers with data center capabilities accumulated in Korea and proved its business competitiveness in the global market." CEO Hyun added, "We will use this as a bridgehead to expand AI data centers and AI factory businesses in global markets including Asia-Pacific, where demand for AI computing is rapidly increasing."
